title: Find and replace a failing jar in battery string 3 (UPS bank A)
summary: Path A runs normally on utility. The string monitor of the UPS A battery room raises a float current alarm on string 3: one jar in that string is failing and heating. Find it before it reaches thermal runaway. In the battery room (field view, BATTERY): scan string 3 with the infrared camera, confirm the jar with the battery analyzer (voltage and internal ohmic value), then take the string off line in OSHA order: open the string disconnect SB3, apply your padlock, split the string at its mid-string link (the string is a 542 V source by itself), replace the jar, put the link back, remove your padlock and close SB3. The other three strings keep the UPS protected meanwhile. If the jar reaches 60 C it vents and the drill ends.
references: Operator master specification (digital twin EPMS), subsystem 4: 4 strings of 40 jars, 542.1 VDC, infrared (ironbow) and impedance analyzer, example jar 18 of string 3 at 48.6 C, 14.2 mOhm, 10.4 V; H2 alarm at 1 % LEL

Battcon 2013, 'Batteries die in thirds' (Vertiv): ohmic value changes of 30 % to 50 % and greater over baseline indicate aging and loss of capacity (model thresholds +30 % warn, +50 % replace), checked 2026-11-26
Hydrogen LEL 4 % by volume; IFC / NFPA 1 and NYC MC 502.4.1 limit a VRLA battery room to 1 % hydrogen by volume (25 % LEL) by ventilation, checked 2026-11-26
OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 (d): isolate, apply the lockout device, then release or restrain stored energy; the padlock on SB3 is the employee's own
Model values: float currents, heating rate, 60 C runaway limit, gas evolution and the mid-string link are this simulator's, not a vendor procedure

steps.text: Scan string 3 with the infrared camera
Measure the hot jar with the battery analyzer (jar 18)
Remove the mid-string link of string 3
Link back, padlock off, SB3 closed: string 3 on line
